prompt: Vertical 9:16 editorial wedding-night photograph at high resolution, 100 mm macro-portrait lens at ear height, at a sangeet under a shamiana. The camera is behind a young Indian woman and slightly to the left; her head is turned fully away, so the jaw and cheek are hidden behind the ear and hair; no eyelash, brow, cheek, nose or lip breaks the outline of her head anywhere in the frame (last time her head was only three-quarters away and eyelashes and a brow tail showed past the cheek; never again). Reference 1 is the authority on this exact piece: copy its construction exactly and ignore its background and light. Reference 2 is a detail of the same piece. Ignore the plaster block as well; reference 2 shows the open braid and its see-through core up close. FIDELITY: one hoop on the earlobe nearest the camera: a round hoop 25 mm across, a 5-6 mm open plait, no stones, no bottom loop, 18k gold tone, mirror polish. THE BRAID, copied exactly from reference 2: a chunky, rounded, three-dimensional open plait about 5-6 mm thick, as deep as it is wide; made of many separate, individually rounded, mirror-polished wires laid in pairs, each pair crossing over and under the next in chevrons; between the outer wires you can see straight through to an inner core of finer wires and to the skin behind; every wire carries its own bright highlight. It is NOT a flat three-strand ribbon braid, NOT bundles of parallel grooved or brushed wires, NOT engraved lines, NOT a smooth tube, NOT a twisted rope (last time it came out as a flat three-strand ribbon plait of grouped, parallel, grooved satin wires; that is wrong). THE DISC: exactly ONE flat, round, mirror-polished disc, about one third of the hoop's width, on the latch end only, where the hoop meets the earlobe on the side away from the hinge; the other end is a small cylindrical hinge knuckle with NO disc. Never two discs (last time a second disc was invented on the hinge end). THE LATCH: one thin curved latch wire swings from the hinge knuckle, passes through the earlobe piercing and clicks into the catch behind the disc, so the hoop is one closed ring hanging from the lobe; no gap in the ring, no loose stubs, no small loops or jump rings (last time each end had its own stub, nothing passed through the lobe and the hoop was an open C hanging from nothing). Mirror polish, warm-neutral 18k gold tone, never satin, brushed or matte. It must stay a many-wire open braid, never a smooth tube, a simple twist or an oval; do not redesign or add anything. SCALE: scale by the ear: the hoop's outer width is a little less than half the ear's height from the top of the ear to the tip of the lobe; two hoops stacked would not reach the top of the ear; the hoop is about the size of a 25 mm coin (last time the hoop was drawn at 0.59 of the ear's height, about 1.35 times too big). Field of view about 11 cm wide, so the hoop is about 23% of the frame's width and the whole ear fits in frame; a soft contact shadow where it touches the neck. BODY: the ear sits just left of the frame's centre on the left outline of her head; beyond the ear on the left only out-of-focus background, never a cheek; the back of her head, smooth black hair and a low bun fill the right side; bare nape with fine downy hair, an ivory raw-silk blouse collar low in frame. THE AUNTY: from the left edge, an older Indian woman's hand, about sixty, warm brown skin with soft creases, short bare nails, no rings, bangles, watch or mehendi, the wrist under a rani-pink silk pallu, holds a complete pair of dark tortoiseshell half-moon reading glasses: two flat-topped half-moon lenses joined by a thin bridge, two temple arms; she holds them by one folded temple arm, the bridge and far lens toward the left edge; the near lens is in FRONT of the hoop, about 8 cm from it, between the camera and the hoop, its flat top edge level across the middle of the hoop so it covers the hoop's lower half, the lens about 40% of the frame's width; nothing of the hoop passes in front of the frame; the rim never crosses the disc or the latch (last time the glasses were a round full-rim frame with one lens, no bridge and a hinge at both ends, and the hoop threaded through the rim; never again). The glass is perfectly clear, showing what is behind it at the same size, undistorted and untinted, with no haze and no reflection streak, reflecting nothing, never a face or eyes. WORLD: a plum-dark shamiana at night, soft marigold fairy-light bokeh. COMPOSITION AND PLACEMENT: the disc at about 36% of the frame height, the hoop's bottom and the lens's lower rim no lower than 52%, so hoop and lens sit between 33% and 53% of the frame height (last time they sat too low, at 47-61%); from 14% to 32%, on the left and centre, calm out-of-focus plum bokeh with soft marigold points and nothing else, kept clear for the headline; below 55% only soft ivory silk and plum shadow, darker toward the bottom, kept calm and clear for the price card, with the aunty's wrist and pink sleeve kept to the left edge. LIGHT: soft warm fill from the fairy lights above left; one small hard specular kicker from behind right puts a crisp highlight on every polished wire of the braid and on the disc. Warm-neutral 18k gold tone, never brassy or orange. NEGATIVES: no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark anywhere; no face, no eyes, no eyelashes, no eyebrows anywhere, never reflected in the lens; one product only: no second earring, necklace or nose pin; no second disc, no jump rings, no gap in the hoop; no round or full-rim glasses; no rings or bangles on anyone; no star-shaped glints.
